- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, cap the overshoot at 2–3% above recent peak.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.25.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward mean reversion (e.g., 10–15% correction toward prior 14-day average).
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
